cards.a: Filters that match routes by prefix and prefix-length, the preferred way to match routes in BGP policy (route-maps, distribute-lists, filters) because they are faster and cleaner than access-lists for routing. The exam focuses on the ge and le modifiers and first-match-wins evaluation order.

cards.q: What is the prefix list syntax?
cards.a: ip prefix-list NAME {seq} deny|permit PREFIX/LEN [ge GE] [le LE]. Without ge or le, only an exact prefix of that length matches.

cards.q: What are the implicit prefix list rules?
cards.a: Default len is only the stated length; default ge equals the stated length; default le is 32; matching requires the prefix bits be identical AND the length be within [ge, le]; and an implicit deny applies at the end so nothing matches beyond the configured entries.

cards.q: What does ip prefix-list FOO permit 10.0.0.0/8 ge 16 le 24 match?
cards.a: It matches 10.0.0.0/8 prefixes with lengths from 16 through 24 only; a /25 or longer is not matched. ge and le modify length, not the prefix bits, and the /8 prefix part stays fixed.

cards.q: What matches permit 0.0.0.0/0 le 32 and permit 0.0.0.0/0?
cards.a: 0.0.0.0/0 le 32 matches everything, the universal permit commonly placed at the end of lists; 0.0.0.0/0 alone matches only the default route.

cards.q: How are prefix list entries evaluated?
cards.a: Sequences are evaluated lowest seq first and the first match wins; an implicit deny is applied at the end no matter what. Prefix lists support sequence numbers that can be reordered or deleted.

cards.q: How do you use a prefix list inside a route-map or directly on a neighbor?
cards.a: Reference it with match ip address prefix-list UPSTREAM inside a route-map, or apply it directly with neighbor ... prefix-list NAME {in|out}.
show ip prefix-list, show ip prefix-list detail, and show ip prefix-list NAME sum display the configured lists and their counters.

cards.q: Why might a prefix list filter out every route by accident?
cards.a: Because of the implicit deny at the end. If a final permit such as 0.0.0.0/0 le 32 is missing, anything not explicitly matched is denied.

cards.q: Does a prefix list auto-include longer prefixes of the stated network?
cards.a: No. The stated /len is the only anchor; longer prefixes are included only if le (or a ge/le range) allows them. The longest-prefix behaviour of routing does not apply to matching.
